newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FAI sees continued profit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FAI sees continued profit growth.

text.p: FAI Insurances Ltd said on Wednesday that it expected to continue the profit growth which resulted in first half net profit rising by 35.4 percent to A$7.7 million.
"FAI considers the results for the previous half year pleasing," chief executive Rodney Adler said of the latest period.

"Subject to economic conditions not declining and in the absence of abnormal events in the insurance field, we believe the growth in profitability will be maintained," Adler said in a statement accompanying the first half profit result.
The company said its underwriting loss in the latest half ended December 31 rose to A$38 million from a loss of A$21.9 million a year ago.

"The increase in our underwriting loss was primarily caused by the reduction in the discount gap calculated by our actuaries in determining our long tail insurance reserves. The drop in the discount gap was due primarily to the fall in interest rates during the period which resulted in a A$24 million increase in our insurance reserves," FAI said.
FAI said it held cash and liquid securities of A$401 million at balance date.
"It is our current intention to maintain high cash balances and a relatively low investment in the equities market," the company said.
Premium income net of reinsurance fell 4.75 percent to A$306.5 million from A$321.9 million a year ago, with the fall mostly due to competition in the commercial insurance sector.
FAI also said the contribution from wholly-owned Oceanic Coal Australia Ltd was lower due to the geology of the area now being mined.

"Due to a drop in coal prices and a strengthening Australian dollar, we anticipate a continued deterioration in this subsidiary and are not confident of its profit performance in the current year," it said.
FAI shares were two cents higher at 72 cents at 2.56 p.m. (0356 GMT).
